_scope: THIS PROJECT's use of a bench: which bench, what stands on it and where. Separate from the bench file on purpose - see bench.json's _scope.
_PROVISIONAL_2026_07_27: Kyle re-cabled the cell today (cameras onto a powered hub, a second camera added, and a longer arm control cable so it no longer crosses the work area) and said a full reorganisation is coming: 'for now all positions are provisional'. So EVERY position below is now UNVERIFIED, including ones that were measured, and `sim.simcam` renders from these numbers - it will show a view the real camera does not have until they are re-measured. Do not treat a simcam frame as predicting what the bench camera sees until this key is gone. What is NOT invalidated: camera INTRINSICS (a property of lens and sensor, not of position), the collision gate, IK, and the motion work - none of those depend on where anything sits.

arm._comment: Arm base centre. x 51.5 = 24 on centre from the main table edge (x 27.5), measured along the return; y 20.25 puts it on the return's front edge. yaw -90: the arm is aligned with the table edge and REACHES TOWARD THE WALL (Kyle), which is the -y direction from the front edge to the side wall at y=0. Convention: 0 = reaches along +x, positive counter-clockwise from above, so -90 = reaches along -y. Pinned by _selftest_arm_frame, because a 90-degree error here looks plausible and silently rotates the entire cell about the arm. ASSUMPTION still open: 'on the front edge' taken as the base CENTRE on the edge line; if the base plate is flush with the edge, the centre is inboard by half the base.

cameras.name: side
cameras.notes: SECOND CAMERA, added 2026-07-27. Position deliberately NULL rather than guessed: it is registered and streaming (cameras.json, hub port 3) and its first frame shows a low view across the bench from table level, but nobody has measured where it is. Nulls here mean the sim will not draw it, which is the correct behaviour - an invented pose would render a sight line that looks like evidence. Fill in after the reorganisation. A low angle is worth keeping wherever it lands: the overhead camera cannot resolve HEIGHT above the table and this one can, which is what a grasp approach needs.

render._comment: Shadows OFF by default (Kyle, 2026-07-26) until the lighting is right - hard shadows over a half-built room read as geometry errors that are not there. Flip to true to experiment.
